newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower but ENI holds its own.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower but ENI holds its own.

text.p: Italian stocks ended lower in thin trading on Monday but shares in energy giant ENI, trading today after a successful second tranche offering, closed positive despite paring gains towards the close, traders said.
Italian bond futures' weakness weighed on the market which was low on liquidity and "a bit in the doldrums, only kept going by the focus on ENI," one trader said.
ENI closed 0.28 percent up at 7,190 lire.
The All-share Mibtel index ended 0.4 percent down at 9788 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 0.43 percent off at 14,719.
Total traded volume was estimated at around 525 billion lire, little changed from Friday, with ENI trade accounting for about one third of all the business.
ENI opened at 7,200 lire and touched a day's peak at 7,315, and low of 7,165, in volume of over 25 million shares.

Fiat lost 2.89 percent to 4,095 lire, insurer Generali fell 1.99 percent to 29,960 and in banks, Banca Commerciale Italiana slipped 1.95 percent to 2,711 and investment bank Mediobanca lost 2.0 percent to 8,128. Telecoms were mixed, with Telecom Italia and Stet holding gainers but mobile phone operator TIM lost 0.45 percent to 3,115. Olivetti was 0.94 pct off at 453.3.
